source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt treats the invoice itself as sufficient authority to change vendor bank details ('If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record'), with no requirement to verify the change through a channel independent of the invoice.

The sole safeguard on an irreversible payment or bank-detail change is an instruction to request approval 'with a one line summary,' i.e., safety depends on what the model chooses to disclose in that summary, and the approver never sees raw bank account data or change history.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a model-generated one-line summary, not the raw bank account number, the diff from the record on file, or the invoice itself. A more capable or more persuasive model can write a summary that is technically accurate but omits the fraud-relevant fact of a bank-detail change (ASI09, SAFE-T1403). High daily approval volume (~150/day) compounds this with approval fatigue.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of new bank details
controls.decay_rationale: Verification through a channel not sourced from the invoice (e.g., a callback to a phone number already on file prior to the invoice) cannot be spoofed by model behavior or invoice content, so it does not decay with capability.

controls.name: Payment destination confirmation bound to a previously verified vendor record
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the payment destination check to a bank record verified before the most recent unverified change prevents payment to a freshly, unverifiedly changed account regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Summary-gated approval (TC9) lets an untrusted invoice drive an irreversible bank change and payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice content, including a claimed new bank account, enters the agent.
Agent reads the current vendor master record to match the invoice.
Agent updates vendor bank details based solely on invoice content (prompt.md line 2), gated only by ctl.clerk_approval.
Agent schedules an irreversible payment, potentially to the just-changed bank account, gated only by ctl.clerk_approval.

forecast.watch_signal: Platform model version changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true, already true today); clerk approval volume rising further above ~150/day; or the approval UI being simplified to reduce clicks per card — any of these indicates the summary-only gate is approaching rubber-stamping.

evidence.observation: Agent updates the vendor bank record whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details,' with no independent verification source other than the invoice itself.
The only stated safeguard for payment or bank change is a clerk approval based on 'a one line summary,' i.e., a model-generated summary rather than raw data.
The sample card shows only vendor name, amount, invoice id, and PO match — no bank account number and no indication that a bank detail change occurred.

Bank account numbers and change history are explicitly not shown to the clerk; the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (credential_scope: broad); the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the model_upgrade trigger is effectively already live.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification of any new bank details (e.g., a callback to a phone number already on file prior to the invoice, never a contact supplied by the invoice) before cap.bank_update is applied, independent of model or clerk judgment.

Change the approval card to raw_action review: show the clerk the actual current vs. proposed bank account number, the change history, and the source invoice, not only a one-line model-generated summary.

Scope the ERP credential so the agent cannot both write vendor bank details and schedule payment under the same broad credential; require least-privilege, separately-approved credentials for bank-detail writes.
Alert when a payment is scheduled to a bank account that differs from the account on file, or when a bank-detail change and a payment to that same vendor occur within one processing cycle.

rating.rationale: One finding drives the rollup. Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted, externally-authored invoice (in.supplier_invoice) reaches two S3 sinks — a configure-class bank-detail write (cap.bank_update) and an irreversible spend (cap.schedule_payment) — both under a broad ERP credential. The only declared control, ctl.clerk_approval, is a structural human gate but is scored partially_dependent because the approver sees only a model-written one-line summary, not the bank account number or change history (approval_review_mode: model_summary). Per rubric section 5 step 2, this earns a 2-tier credit with a floor of moderate, giving residual = moderate, exactly at the floor. Because subject.model.swappable is true and the platform upgrades the model with no separate review, the model_upgrade trigger that defeats model_summary approval gates is effectively already active: a more persuasive model can write a summary that is accurate but omits the fraud-relevant fact, which is the ASI09/SAFE-T1403 mechanism. The stated approval volume (~150 cards/day) independently makes autonomy_increase and longer_task_horizon plausible degradation paths for the same gate (approval fatigue). Once ctl.clerk_approval is defeated, no other control remains on the path — there is no out-of-band bank-detail verification and no destination confirmation bound to a prior verified record — so the forecast reverts to the inherent tier of critical. The autonomy modifier (unspecified step/runtime limits) was considered but has no visible effect since inherent is already at the maximum tier.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, the sample approval card, and the provided runtime notes. It does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP configuration, IaC, or tool manifest was provided; credential_scope and capability boundaries are inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so confidence on the exact credential boundary is medium even though confidence in the overall finding is high.

Autonomy level (A2) is inferred from the prompt's approval instruction rather than from an orchestration/runtime config; whether the approval step actually blocks execution in the deployed system should be verified.
The attack path is limited to 4 steps, within the rubric's 6-step search limit.
